scope: Follow-up to early-wny-source-review-2026-11-15.json: contemporary Buffalo refinery listings, Buffalo and Akron cement processes, and Bolivar map coverage.
editorialDisposition: Expand /research/early-industry to nine chapters. Add a distinct Buffalo cement chapter, an 1873 Buffalo refining chapter, a historical quarry photograph and a Bolivar coverage finding. Retain uncertain footprints without precise map pins. Deployment must be checked separately.

sources.title: Lime and Cement Industries of New York
sources.author: Heinrich Ries
sources.publisher: New York State Museum Bulletin 44, 1901 volume, with a January 1902 editorial revision noted on printed page 838
sources.locators: Printed 836 / PDF 377: Akron; printed 837 / PDF 388: Buffalo; plate 84 / PDF 387: Buffalo Cement quarry photograph.
sources.review: Downloaded original scan and OCR; rendered and visually checked printed pages 836 and 837 and plate 84. Archive leaf numbers differ from PDF page numbers; original images establish the locators.
findings: Buffalo Cement Company quarries were on Main Street near the New York Central Belt Line. Ten firebrick-lined stone kilns in two rows received rock and coke via an inclined haulage system. Grinding and screening separated material; clinker went to a Griffin mill for a product described as Portland cement. Reported capacity about 750 barrels daily.
Plate 84 credits L. P. Bishop and identifies the quarry railway as carrying stone to the crusher.
Cummings at Akron had seventeen kilns, crushers, pulverizers and millstones; Union Akron was another large works. The original reads 575 acres. OCR readings suggesting other acreage must not be used.
limits: Turn-of-century descriptions do not date all machinery to the founding years.
Capacity is not measured output or an emission quantity.
The survey does not establish current contamination, quarry fill contents or modern parcel boundaries.

sources.title: The Early and Later History of Petroleum
sources.author: J. T. Henry
sources.publisher: Philadelphia: J. B. Rodgers Co., 1873; University of California Libraries copy
sources.review: Downloaded original scan and OCR; rendered and visually checked the Buffalo entries. The printed Dudley capacity is 251, not an assumed correction to 250.
findings: Star Oil Works, Thayer & Riddell, 385 Hamburg Street, nearly 200 barrels daily still capacity.
Dudley & Co., 251 barrels daily still capacity; some refining done at Miller Farm on Oil Creek before shipment to Buffalo.
limits: No evidence identifies either firm as the receiver of recovered Bolivar creek oil.
Company capacity is not necessarily all located in Buffalo.
Historical street numbering needs a modern geographic crosswalk before mapping.

unresolved: Herrick's Empire Oil (1949) original passage has not been read; DEC and local retellings should not count as fully independent confirmations.
Cynthia exact footprint and the Buffalo consignee remain unverified. Deeds, siding plans and shipping records would be useful.
Granger's Forest Lawn works and Buffalo Cement's Main Street/Belt Line operation remain distinct; quarry photos do not alone establish modern parcel boundaries.
